| Failure mode: the cabin door unlocks while the cabin is in motion. Effect: a passenger falls onto the guideway. Cause: failure of the locking monitor, or faulty evaluation of the standstill signal. | 10 | 2 | 2 | 40 | `REQ-mit-dual-channel-locking` | ✗ |

| Failure mode: a cabin locked out for maintenance is dispatched despite the lockout. Effect: a trip with incompletely tested equipment. Cause: the lockout record is lost when the fleet control system restarts. | 5 | 3 | 3 | 45 | `REQ-mit-lockout-survives-restart` | ✗ |
| Failure mode: the cabin reports a normal operating state while the lockout record says the cabin is locked out. Cause: the lockout state is carried in SCHEMA-lockout-record, held by the fleet control system, and again as operating state in SCHEMA-cabin-state, held by the cabin controller; the two are maintained separately. | Failure mode: both positioning sources fail and the cabin position is undetermined. Effect: the affected section comes to a standstill, or an unsafe block clearance is granted. Cause: a common cause in the power supply of the positioning sensors. | 7 | 3 | 2 | 42 | `REQ-mit-separate-power-for-positioning` | ✗ |

| Failure mode: FUNC-check-service-readiness answers ready from an operational picture that is out of date. Effect: a cabin is dispatched to a station that has meanwhile gone out of service; the passenger waits at a closed platform and a platform slot is blocked. Cause: FLOW-operational-picture is imported from another chain; REQ-picture-freshness binds the age of the displayed picture, nothing binds the consumer to reject a stale one. | 4 | 4 | 3 | 48 | `REQ-mit-readiness-freshness-check` | ✗ |
| Failure mode: the door pair is released on a standstill proof that no longer holds. Effect: doors open while the cabin is still creeping; a passenger falls into the platform gap. Cause: the standstill proof is carried twice, in SCHEMA-door-command and in SCHEMA-door-release, produced in two different chains and two different modules; nothing requires the two copies to agree or bounds their age. | 10 | 2 | 4 | 80 | `REQ-mit-single-standstill-proof` | ✗ |
| Failure mode: a function receives a value in a state field that it does not expect and behaves in an undefined way. Effect: undefined behaviour inside a safety chain, and no test can tell a valid transition from an invalid one. Cause: all 32 SCHEMA elements describe their fields in prose and enumerate no values; fields such as occupancy state, operating state, door state, obstruction state, energization state, release state, lockout state, command type and display priority carry no value list. This is a single system-wide finding, not one per schema. | 8 | 5 | 8 | 320 | `REQ-mit-enumerated-state-values` | ✗ |
